correctness.rationale: Exact normalized cosine projection formula differentiates a unit-step response as 2 sin(m pi s)sin(m pi x)+2 sin(3m pi s)sin(3m pi x). Absolute kernel periodicity removes the frequency. For u=cos^2(m pi s), the output variation equals (2/pi)sqrt(1-u)I(4u-1). Convexity of I on [-1,-1/3], direct positive-integrand integration on [-1/3,1], and the explicit upper bound on [1,3] strictly exclude u>0. The maximizer u=0 yields (16 sqrt(2)-8)/(3 pi). Signed derivative-measure decomposition into jumps proves the universal BV inequality, and unit jumps at odd half-periods attain it. Numeric tests corroborate but are not used for infinite quantifiers.

value.rationale: Real frequency-selective rank-three Neumann cosine projection is a natural sparse approximation operator, whose exact BV edge-amplification cost is not its L2 norm. The norm is unexpectedly independent of the harmonic frequency m and all sharp single jumps are centered in odd half-periods, whereas the full cubic spectral cutoff moves extremizers off center. These provide a precise benchmark for jump-bearing data and reveal the effect of deleting the even second harmonic, with no claim of universal significance for arbitrary frequency sets.
